REMOVAL_OF_THE_FROZEN_DEPLOYMENT_TREE.why_this_record_exists_and_why_it_is_com: RULING-20260819-lanec-issue54-frozen-deployment.md states: 'Authorization receipts are committed before they are acted on, and this document is a ruling, not a receipt.' Its section 6 also lists 'any deletion or top-level reorg' among things NOT authorised, and that clause is not limited to repo content. So the removal needed an authorization of its own and this is it, landed before the act rather than after.
REMOVAL_OF_THE_FROZEN_DEPLOYMENT_TREE.what_this_does_NOT_do_to_the_protected_c: The same ruling forbids 'altering 377c713d's citation in the addendum, the active-run receipt, or the armed watch's context, ON THE GROUNDS OF THIS DEFECT'. This annotation is on different grounds (Joseph's removal authorization) and is STRICTLY ADDITIVE: deployment.path and deployment.commit are byte-identical to their pre-annotation values, asserted by a diff in the committing lane's transcript. Nothing here re-cuts or repoints anything.
REMOVAL_OF_THE_FROZEN_DEPLOYMENT_TREE.why_that_route_is_sufficient: 377c713d is an ancestor of pushed main (predicate chosen because it reproduces from a fresh clone; per-checkout ref counts do not, and two lanes measured 23-32 vs 16-25 for the same commits). deployment.commit above records the full 40-hex sha, so the tree is reconstructable without this receipt being changed further.
REMOVAL_OF_THE_FROZEN_DEPLOYMENT_TREE.and_what_it_is_NOT: A surviving RECONSTRUCTION route is not a surviving REFERENCE. Once the directory is gone, this receipt's deployment.path names a path that does not exist until someone runs the command above. That is the whole reason this annotation is required rather than optional, and it is why the path field was left intact instead of being blanked.
